neighbours.label: '-y' adjective formed from a nature noun inside a proper place or institution name (Ston|y Brook, Mist|y Fjords, Sunnyvale, Rocky Mountains), vs place names built from the bare noun
fire: The ferry from Misty Harbor leaves twice a day in summer.
He grew up in a small town near Stony Point on the Hudson.
The park rangers at Rocky Gap closed the trail for the winter.
The startup moved its offices to Sunnyvale last spring.
We camped two nights near Mossy Creek before heading north.
Her cousin teaches at Windy Ridge Elementary School.
The resort at Snowy Peak opens in early December.
She took the bus to Stony Creek to visit her aunt.
quiet: The ferry from Stone Harbor leaves twice a day in summer.
He grew up in a small town near West Point on the Hudson.
The park rangers at Rock Island closed the trail for the winter.
The startup moved its offices to Sun Valley last spring.
We camped two nights near Moss Landing before heading north.
Her cousin teaches at Wind River Elementary School.
The resort at Snow Peak opens in early December.
She took the bus to Stone Creek to visit her aunt.

predictions: Place names with a -y nature adjective reach 0.4-0.9; the matching bare-noun place names (Stone Harbor, Sun Valley) stay under 0.15.
short: -y nature word in a place name
notes: Card: Rock|y Mountain, Ston|y Brook x3, SUN|NY|VALE, st|ony, Woody, Zaryab. Probe: Stony Brook 0.864, Sunnyvale 0.763, Rocky Mountains 0.396, snowy ridge 0.342, stony road 0.223, windy/misty 0.190; muddy 0.118, no -y word 0.002-0.013.
